name: How Long Do Driveway Permits Take in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: How long does a driveway contractor permit take in Los Angeles County for a new driveway or driveway replacement?
mainEntity.text: How long does a driveway contractor permit take in Los Angeles County for a new driveway or driveway replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timeline depends on where the property is located in Los Angeles County and what the driveway work includes. A like-for-like replacement may be straightforward, but new driveways, widened driveways, or work near the curb often trigger extra review for grading, drainage, accessibility, or public works approvals. In many cities, the fastest way to avoid delays is to have a contractor prepare a complete submittal package before demolition starts. That package may include site measurements, material specifications, drainage details, and photos of the existing conditions. If the project affects the sidewalk, curb, or gutter, the approval process can take longer because additional departments may need to review it. Homeowners should also ask whether inspections are required before pour day, after base preparation, and after final completion. A contractor experienced in Los Angeles County should be able to estimate the permit path early and flag any city-specific issues that could change the schedule.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permit timelines in Los Angeles County vary by city, scope, and whether the project affects the public right-of-way, curb, or sidewalk. Simple replacements can move faster than new driveways, but approvals may take longer if grading, drainage, or apron work is involved. A contractor should confirm the local permit office, required plans, and inspection sequence before starting.
